meaning: Isurus, from Greek ísos “equal” + ourá “tail”, for caudal-fin lobes described as equal in length (the upper is in fact clearly longer); oxyrinchus, Greek for “sharp-snouted” (oxýs “sharp” + rhýnchos “snout”), for its pointed snout
description: A torpedo-shaped open-ocean shark with a pointed snout, large black eyes and a crescent tail. Its back is metallic blue, cut off sharply from a white underside. It hunts fast-moving fish and squid in warm and temperate seas worldwide.
depth: Surface to about 150 m, rarely deeper
